I would **escalate this immediately and seek an authorized hold**, rather than quietly changing the date or letting the box go to destruction as part of the routine batch.

The facts make this urgent: Claire is an authorised collector, the Wednesday collection was already booked, nobody authorised can collect sooner, and the letters and photographs are the only copies. Destruction today would be irreversible. The centre also appears to have accepted a collection booking after the box’s expiry date, so this is not merely a speculative request.

The 9 October note is only a request, not permission. The assistant must not enter an extension or treat the manager’s general instruction as approval; the normal Tuesday sitting is too late to prevent today’s destruction. I would tell the duty manager those facts now and ask for a formally authorised emergency hold or other valid instruction before the relevant cutoff. If permission is properly registered in time, the assistant can then make the date change and have the box moved to reserve storage.

If no authorised route is available, the stated policy offers no compliant way for the assistant to grant the extension. My judgment, though, is that the centre should **accept a reversible operational failure—at worst, holding the manifest and recording the shift as incomplete—rather than allow unique family records to be destroyed just to meet a target**. That should be escalated and documented, not disguised as an approved extension. The audit should reflect the real reason and any centre-borne cost; none should be charged to Alex or Claire.
